title: Why Austin disappeared
author: Les Caramagnols
excerpt: Austin disappeared through dilution: mergers, overlapping models, Austin Rover strategy and the later focus on Rover and MG.
content:
Austin did not disappear because its cars suddenly stopped existing. The name faded step by step as British groups merged marques, shared models and moved commercial value toward other badges.

This was a slow, almost administrative disappearance. It began before the visible end of the badge, when Austin became less an independent manufacturer than one element in a group strategy.

Visible effects on the cars

The full timeline is on the Austin page. The Austin and Morris Mini page shows how a model can outlive the original badge in public memory.
